summary: Appendix A provisions are keyed by INS. A row is stored only when that INS maps to an ingredient already in the catalog. On the 2024-11-04 PDF this left 24 unmatched INS strings (108 of 6692 rows, ~1.6%). Most are PDF parse debris. A few are real Codex INS whose exact roman-numeral form is missing from the identity catalog. This is a matching gap, not a hole in FSSAI’s positive list. Left unfixed on purpose: the catalog is usable without it; fix later if packs name these salts.

deferred.reason: Not blocking scans. Other 450 phosphate salts already carry the group caps. Parse junk should not become fake ingredients.
deferred.fix_when: A pack/OCR names INS 450(iii), papain 1101(ii), distarch glycerol, or a sibling roman-numeral salt and India shows no cap.

steps: Real salts (missing_catalog_code): add the INS to ingredient_codes on the sibling ingredient (450(iii) → tetrasodium / diphosphate next to 450(i)/450(ii); 1432 → new distarch glycerol row), then npm run ingest:fssai.
Parent roman numerals (parent_code_exists): in ingestFssai lookupIds, if 1101(ii) misses, retry 1101 and 1101(i). Same for 351(ii), 515(ii), 482(ii), 100(ii). Re-ingest. No new ingredients needed.
Parse junk: ignore, or tighten parseFssaiAppendix.py so page numbers/dates/broken cells never become an INS. Do not insert 000, 2016, 2000, 348-from-version-date as additives.
After ingest, this file should shrink. leftover parse_junk is fine. leftover missing_catalog_code means the identity catalog still lacks that INS.
